label: flint-kapitsa
note: Kapitsa's defaults on Recursive's MLX 4-bit export (RecursiveSI/flint-int4, `kapitsa pull flint`): plain decoding (Flint has no drafter; prompt lookup is off by default). Sampling at Flint's recommended temperature 1.0 (top_p 0.95, top_k 20) for every engine. Flint reasons before every answer with no switch for it, so bench.py runs with --always-reasons (the reasoning is the reply's first part, its tokens counted), and its reference prompt tokens (4000: 3874, 16000: 15066) are Flint's chat template rendered by transformers' apply_chat_template and tokenized by tokenizers 0.23.3, the median of 8 nonces (3872-3877, 15065-15068). --slots 1 for parity with the others' single sequence. The SSD prefix cache is a folder in the harness state, emptied before and after each run.

label: flint-rec
note: Recursive's own engine (recursive-oss/rec v0.1.0, its release binary: a Go launcher over rec-mlx, MLX 0.32 with a resident decode megakernel), `rec serve` as its README runs it, on the same int4 files (APFS clones in the folder rec keeps its pinned manifest's files in, so nothing is downloaded or copied), under a short XDG_DATA_HOME (~/.cache/kbr): rec's unix socket lives there and a socket path is limited to 104 bytes. --context 32768 as Kapitsa's --ctx. Its key file holds a fixed local token (32 bytes as hex) that the harness sends; the first start verifies every file's SHA-256 (ready_timeout 1800).

label: flint-llamacpp
note: llama-server (a build with Flint support: b11804; LLAMA_SERVER names it) on Recursive's Q4_1 GGUF for llama.cpp on Metal, with the flags of its model card (-ngl all, F16 KV, --cache-ram 0, Flint's sampling) except -b/-ub 2048, the 2048-token prefill chunks the other engines use (the card's 256 / 128 were measured too: see the result notes), and -c 32768 -np 1 as the others.
